t: Except as provided in this Act, all laws and parts of laws in conflict with the provisions of this Act are hereby suspended to the extent of such conflict for the period in which this Act shall be in force.

fable.w: This is a boilerplate conflict-of-laws clause that suspends inconsistent laws while the Act is in force. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. There is no tempting contrary reading, since nothing in the text is on-topic for participation.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard savings clause or suspension clause that addresses the legal hierarchy and applicability of existing laws relative to the new Act. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in the decision-making process. It is purely a statement of statutory effect.
qwen_block.s: Except as provided in this Act, all laws and parts of laws in conflict with the provisions of this Act are hereby suspended to the extent of such conflict for the period in which this Act shall be in force.

No one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision, and there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Reading anything procedural into 'Except as provided in this Act' fails because the clause only governs how this Act relates to other laws.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** This is a standard conflict-of-laws clause. It suspends conflicting laws while the Act is in force. The only possible temptation is the phrase "Except as provided in this Act," and it does not hold up: nothing here involves consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies, rulemaking or a right to sue.
